p: he spake a parable unto them: God will have us to continue in prayer, not to weary us, but to exercise us; therefore we must fight against impatience so that a long delay does not cause us to quit our praying.
faint: Yield to afflictions and adversities as those do who have lost heart.

Saying: He does not compare things that are of equal stature, but the less with the greater: If a man receives what is rightfully his at the hands of a most unrighteous judge, much more will the prayers of the godly prevail before God.

weary me: Literally, "beat me down with her blows", and it is a metaphor taken of wrestlers who beat their adversaries with their fists or clubs: in the same way those that are persistent beat the judge's ears with their crying out, even as it were with blows.
he bear long with them: Though he seems slow in avenging the harm done to his own.

And he spake this parable unto: Two things especially make our prayers void and of no effect: confidence of our own righteousness, and our contempt of others; but a humble heart is contrary to both of these.

The Pharisee stood and prayed thus: Although we confess that whatever we have, we have it from God, yet we are despised by God as proud and arrogant if we put even the least trust in our own works before God.
afar off: Far from the Pharisee in a lower place.
And they brought unto him also: The children were tender and young in that they were brought, which appears more evidently in that they were infants. (Ed.)
but when his disciples saw it: To judge or think of Christ after the reason of the flesh is the cause of infinite corruptions.
But Jesus: The elect children of the faithful are included in the free covenant of God. (Ed.)
called them unto him: Those that carried the children, whom the disciples drove away.
Verily I say unto you: Childlike innocence is an ornament of Christians.
And he said: The enticement of riches carries many away from the right way.
And when Jesus saw that he: To be both rich and godly is a singular gift of God.
And he said unto them: They become the richest of all who do not refuse to be poor for Christ's sake.
Then he took unto him the: As sure and certain as persecution is, so sure is the glory which remains for the conquerors.
none of these things: By this we see how ignorant the disciples were.
And it came to pass: Christ shows by a visible miracle that he is the light of the world.
And they which went before rebuked: The more snares and hindrances that Satan lays in our way, even by those who profess Christ's name, so much the more ought we to go forward.
